title: FROZEN objective rubrics for Standard-evaluation metrics scored under normalization family G

spec_reference.note: Family G metric scores are the rubric-defined level score itself. The rubric output IS the 0-100 normalized score. No further normalization (no family C/D rescaling, no min-max, no percentile, no log) is applied to any metric in this document.

fairness_declaration.derivation_prohibition: No rubric level, indicator, threshold, domain, capability, query string, recipe or probe in this document was derived from Quidra's syntax, operators, type system, standard library, tooling, or feature set. Every indicator names a capability that exists independently in multiple mainstream language families and is stated in language-neutral terms (spec 32, 6.1.7). Two channels through which such a derivation could previously have occurred have been closed: the Ecosystem Breadth keyword list is now enumerated in this frozen document instead of being written at collection time, and evidence is now collected with Quidra LAST (global_rules.evidence_collection_order) instead of first.
fairness_declaration.no_young_language_allowance: There is no age adjustment, incumbency discount, maturity handicap, curve, bonus, or compensating term anywhere in this document. Quidra 0.2.0 is expected to score at or near the bottom level of several ecosystem and maturity rubrics. Per spec section 7 that outcome is correct and must be reported unchanged.
fairness_declaration.no_capability_removal: No capability was removed from any checklist because Quidra lacks it. Capabilities Quidra lacks remain in the checklists and are scored as unsatisfied indicators.
fairness_declaration.symmetry: Every indicator is written so that any of the 10 languages can satisfy or fail it. No indicator is satisfiable by construction for exactly one language, and none is phrased as the absence of a feature that only one language has. Every rule that admits a tool, an implementation, a package index or a command does so through a test stated in general terms and applied to all 10 - never through a property that only one language happens to have.
fairness_declaration.no_incumbency_discount: Per spec section 7, an established language's real advantage in package availability, IDE support, debugger integration, build tooling or release history is scored normally and is never discounted as an 'incumbency effect'. In particular the Tooling, Build / Test Integration and IDE / Editor Support metrics count any tool admissible under global_rules.tool_admissibility_test, including third-party tools that a language's own documentation or CI treats as the way to do the job, rather than only tools published by the language's own project. Restricting those metrics to first-party publishers would have erased exactly the ecosystem those metrics exist to measure.
fairness_declaration.no_results_observed_at_freeze: No score has been computed from this document or from any sibling methodology document. Every threshold, band, recipe, query string and indicator here - including those introduced by the remediation recorded in remediation_changelog - was fixed before any language was measured. This is pre-registration, not post-result formula selection (spec 25.4).
fairness_declaration.na_prohibition: Per spec 25.1.G and spec 26, no metric in this document may be marked N/A for any of the 10 languages. A language that lacks a capability a rubric intentionally tests receives the rubric-defined LOW score for that indicator or level. N/A is permitted in this document only in the single situation defined in global_rules.na_last_resort, which cannot arise from a missing language capability.

scale.levels_per_metric: 6 discrete levels for every metric in this document, with the fixed level score set {0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100}
scale.no_interpolation: Only the six level scores may be awarded. Intermediate values, averages of adjacent levels, half-levels and fractional adjustments are prohibited.
scale.rounding: Level scores are exact integers. Category aggregation per spec 8.1 is performed on these integers and reported to two decimal places.

indicator_model.description: Each metric is defined by a fixed, enumerated set of binary indicators or by fixed quantity bands. The level is determined mechanically by the number of satisfied indicators (or by which band the measured quantity falls into). There is no holistic judgement step anywhere in this document.
indicator_model.satisfied_definition: An indicator is SATISFIED only when the scorer has recorded, in the per-language evidence record, positive evidence of the exact kind named by that indicator's evidence_source. Absence of evidence is never satisfaction.
indicator_model.unverifiable_rule: If an indicator's evidence source cannot be retrieved or the check cannot be executed during the evidence window, the indicator is recorded as NOT SATISFIED with verification_status="unverified" and a free-text reason. This conservative rule is applied identically to all 10 languages, including Quidra.
indicator_model.no_partial_credit: An indicator that is partially satisfied is NOT satisfied. Every conjunctive indicator (one containing AND) requires every conjunct.
indicator_model.monotonicity: Where one indicator subsumes another (for example a count threshold ladder), satisfying the stronger indicator does not automatically satisfy the weaker one; the scorer records each independently, and both are expected to be satisfied when the evidence supports it.

evidence_window.rule: Only evidence that existed and was publicly retrievable on or before the evidence cutoff date may be used. Evidence collection itself occurs between the benchmark start date and the completion of Standard scoring; every record carries an accession timestamp and, where applicable, the exact URL or the exact host command executed.
evidence_window.recency_windows: Where an indicator says 'within 24 months' or 'within 90 days', the window ends at the evidence cutoff date 2026-09-17 and is computed from the artifact's published date.

first_party_definition.official_project_set: For each language, 'official', 'first-party' and 'the language's own project' mean any member of that language's official_project_set as frozen in official_project_table below. Nothing outside that set is first-party.
first_party_definition.rationale: Some languages are stewarded by more than one official body (a standards body plus the implementation used here, or a language vendor plus the runtime vendor). Recording the full official set for every language, rather than a single body, prevents an artificial penalty that would come from an arbitrary choice of which official body counts. This rule is applied identically to all 10 languages.
first_party_definition.third_party_rule: Anything published outside the official_project_set is third-party. Third-party evidence may only be used where an indicator explicitly admits it (Library Availability index selection, Ecosystem Breadth packages, Production Adoption, the debugger/profiler indicators that explicitly say 'or named in official documentation', and the indicators listed in global_rules.tool_admissibility_test, which applies a frozen three-clause admissibility test instead of the official_project_set membership test).

tool_admissibility_test.applies_to: Indicators T1-T6 (Tooling), V1-V5 (Build / Test Integration), I1, I4 and I6 (IDE / Editor Support), and the selection of the language server whose published feature list I2 and I3 are scored against. It applies to no other indicator; everywhere else 'first-party' keeps the meaning given in first_party_definition.
tool_admissibility_test.rule: A tool is ADMISSIBLE for one of those indicators if it satisfies at least one of these three clauses: (a) it is published by a member of that language's official_project_set; OR (b) the language's official documentation (E2) names it as a, or the, way to perform the task that indicator describes; OR (c) the official implementation repository's own continuous-integration configuration (E3) invokes it. A tool satisfying none of the three clauses is not admissible and cannot satisfy the indicator.
tool_admissibility_test.recording: For every admissible tool the evidence record states the tool name, its publisher, WHICH CLAUSE it satisfied (a, b or c), and the exact URL plus verbatim excerpt (for clause b, the documentation sentence naming the tool; for clause c, the CI configuration file path and the line that invokes it). A tool admitted without a recorded clause is not admitted.
tool_admissibility_test.why: Spec section 7 forbids discounting an established language's real ecosystem, tooling or maturity advantage as an 'incumbency effect'. Restricting these three metrics to tools published by the official_project_set would have erased exactly the third-party ecosystem that constitutes that advantage: Maven, Gradle and JUnit for Java; CMake, Ninja and googletest for C++; npm and the Node test tooling for TypeScript; Gradle for Kotlin; pip and pytest for Python. Spec section 8 names the metric 'Tooling', not 'First-party Tooling', and spec 25.1.G requires only 'a published objective rubric or proxy with explicit observable criteria'.
tool_admissibility_test.symmetry: The three clauses are language-neutral and are applied identically to all 10 languages, including Quidra. Clause (a) admits a tool a language publishes itself; clauses (b) and (c) admit a tool the language's own documentation or its own CI treats as the way to do the job. Any of the 10 can satisfy or fail each clause. The test neither adds nor removes any indicator; it only fixes which tools may be counted against the indicators that already existed.
tool_admissibility_test.interaction_with_host_presence: Admissibility is a property of the tool, not of this host. Whether an admissible tool is present and runnable here is recorded separately under global_rules.tool_availability_states and affects only the counts that explicitly use it (Tooling H, Package / Dependency Management INSTALLED) and the indicators that require execution.

tool_availability_states.purpose: indicator_model.unverifiable_rule converts every check that cannot be executed on this host into NOT SATISFIED. That rule is uniform in wording but not in effect, because the ten toolchains were provisioned differently (Homebrew repackages, Xcode bundles, one locally built toolchain) and because some tools do not exist for macOS/arm64 at all. Recording WHY a check could not run is therefore mandatory, and two of the counts below are scored on the reason rather than on the bare execution outcome.

states.S1_no_admissible_tool: No tool admissible under tool_admissibility_test exists for this language at the evidence cutoff.
states.S2_official_distribution_but_absent_here: An admissible tool exists AND the language's own official documentation states it ships with the official toolchain distribution, but it is absent from this host's repackaged or bundled install.
states.S3_admissible_but_not_in_distribution_an: An admissible tool exists but is not part of the official toolchain distribution, is not installed on this host, and global_rules.host_verification.no_installation_of_extra_software forbids installing it.
states.S4_blocked_by_host_os: An admissible tool exists but does not run on macOS 26 / arm64 at all.
states.S5_present_and_executed: The tool is present on this host and its documented command was executed, with the output captured.

tool_availability_states.exhaustiveness: Every tool referenced by any indicator is recorded in exactly one of S1-S5. S1 and S5 are the two states the original rule collapsed everything into; S2, S3 and S4 are the three distinguishable non-execution reasons.

scoring_effect.tooling_H: Tooling's H counts a tool in state S5 OR state S2. A tool the language's official documentation states ships with the official distribution counts as present when it is missing here solely because of a repackaged install.
scoring_effect.package_manager_INSTALLED: Package / Dependency Management's INSTALLED is true if the selected manager is in state S5 OR state S2, and false otherwise.
scoring_effect.everything_else: For every indicator whose own text requires a successful execution (for example V3, V4, V5, Q2, Q3, Q4, F2, F4, F5, C1, C5, P3), indicator_model.unverifiable_rule is unchanged: the indicator is NOT SATISFIED with verification_status="unverified". States S2, S3 and S4 do not rescue it; they are published instead.

required_publication.artifact: benchmark/2026-09-17-7677581/standard/rubrics/host_limited_indicators.json, published alongside the Standard results table.
required_publication.contents: Every indicator, for every language, recorded NOT SATISFIED for reason S2, S3 or S4, with the language, metric, indicator id, the state, the tool or command that could not be run, and the reason. Readers can then see exactly which scores are artefacts of how this host was provisioned rather than properties of the language.
required_publication.asymmetry_disclosed: The table must carry this sentence verbatim: 'Quidra's toolchain was built from source on this host by the benchmark team, so no Quidra indicator can fail for a repackaging reason. Indicators that other languages lost to states S2, S3 and S4 are listed below and are host artefacts, not measured language properties.'

host_verification.host: macOS 26.4.1 build 25E253, Darwin 25.4.0, arm64, Apple M2, 8 logical CPUs, 8 GiB RAM
host_verification.rule: Every indicator whose evidence source is E1 must be verified by executing a command on this exact host and preserving the full command line, exit status, stdout and stderr in the per-language evidence record.
host_verification.build_recipes: Measurement of performance, size and any other single-file build or run uses the frozen recipes in environment/environment.json -> frozen_toolchain_recipes, unchanged. Rubric verification uses the frozen, per-language, per-probe-family command lines in this document's rubric_verification_recipes block, and the DIAG probe set uses the frozen warning configuration in the Diagnostics metric's frozen_diagnostic_configuration block. Those two blocks are the ONLY authorised departures from frozen_toolchain_recipes, they were frozen before any language was scored, and no further flag may be added at scoring time. Every command actually executed is recorded verbatim with its exit status, stdout and stderr.
host_verification.no_installation_of_extra_software: Rubric verification must not install software that is not already present on this host. Where an indicator can only be satisfied by software that is not installed, the indicator is evaluated from official documentation evidence (E2/E3) if that indicator admits documentation evidence, and is otherwise recorded as not satisfied with verification_status="unverified" AND with the applicable state from global_rules.tool_availability_states, for publication in the host-limited indicators table.

required_fields: indicators: [{id, satisfied: true|false, verification_status: "verified"|"unverified", evidence_source_id, admissibility_clause: "a"|"b"|"c"|null (required for every indicator listed in global_rules.tool_admissibility_test.applies_to), availability_state: "S1"|"S2"|"S3"|"S4"|"S5"|null (required for every indicator naming a tool or a host command), evidence: {url_or_command, accession_timestamp, quoted_excerpt_or_captured_output, measured_value_if_any}, reason_if_unsatisfied}]
per_language_evidence_record.auditability: A third party holding only this document and the evidence records must be able to recompute every level score without any further judgement.

evidence_collection_order.rule: Evidence is collected in this order, which is NOT the reporting column order in fixed_language_columns. Quidra, the language under evaluation, is collected LAST. No threshold, keyword, query string, procedure or interpretation may be settled after seeing Quidra's result, because every other language has already been recorded by then.
evidence_collection_order.why: The previous rule collected evidence in the fixed column order, in which Quidra is column 1. Anything left to be decided at collection time - most importantly the Ecosystem Breadth keyword list, now frozen below - would have been decided while looking at Quidra first. Collecting Quidra last removes that channel.
evidence_collection_order.applies_to: Every metric in this document, and every probe-set construction step that is not already fully frozen here.

application_order.2: Build the frozen probe sets defined in frozen_probe_sets for all 10 languages, using first-party features only, before any scoring.
application_order.3: Collect evidence per language per metric in the frozen global_rules.evidence_collection_order (Quidra last), recording each indicator independently.
application_order.4: Compute the satisfied count or measured quantity.
application_order.5: Award the unique level whose criteria the count/quantity matches. Levels are mutually exclusive and exhaustive by construction.
application_order.6: Write the evidence record. Do not revisit an earlier language after seeing a later language's score, and do not revise any threshold, keyword, recipe or definition after any language has been scored.

prohibited_at_scoring_time: adding, removing, reordering, reweighting or reinterpreting any indicator
changing any threshold, count band, domain list, capability list or probe
awarding a level whose criteria are not fully met
substituting an evidence source other than the one named for that indicator
marking a metric N/A because a language lacks the tested capability
using a different evidence source, probe, flag, corpus or window for one language than for another
expanding, narrowing or otherwise altering any language's major_implementations list in official_project_table
altering global_rules.evidence_collection_order, or collecting Quidra's evidence before another language's

altering any entry in rubric_verification_recipes, in the Diagnostics metric's frozen_diagnostic_configuration, in the Dependency Simplicity install_units_table, in the Readability frozen_lexing_table, or in the Ecosystem Breadth frozen_query_list
breaking a tie between equal scores by any means (see global_rules.tie_handling)

na_last_resort.only_admissible_case: A metric may be marked N/A for a language only if the measurement host itself made the check impossible for every language simultaneously (for example the frozen probe set could not be built for any language). A single language's lack of a capability, lack of a registry, lack of a debugger, lack of production users, or lack of release history is NEVER N/A: it is the rubric-defined low score.
na_last_resort.if_triggered: Document the reason and apply spec section 26 renormalization within the affected Standard category.

tie_handling.rule: Where two or more languages have identical scores at full precision - on any single metric in this document, on a Standard category score, or on the Standard Overall Score - they are reported at EQUAL RANK with the shared rank number, and no tie-break is applied.
tie_handling.why: With 6 discrete levels {0,20,40,60,80,100} across 17 metrics, exact ties are the expected outcome rather than an edge case. Spec 25.3's rule ('Ranking comparisons use the unrounded values; displayed rounding must not decide ties') does not resolve them, because the unrounded values are genuinely equal. Leaving ties unaddressed would let a tie-break be invented after results are visible, which spec 25.4 forbids.
tie_handling.rank_numbering: Tied languages share the lowest rank number they collectively occupy, and the next distinct score takes the rank equal to the number of languages strictly above it plus one (competition ranking: 1, 2, 2, 4).
tie_handling.prohibited: No secondary metric, no category, no alphabetical order, no column order and no scorer preference may break a tie.

global_rules.aggregation_into_standard_score: Each metric's level score enters its spec-8 category as one equally weighted member, per spec 8.1. This document does not define category or overall weights.

official_project_table._rule: Frozen identity of each language's official project set, official documentation root, official implementation repository, and the implementations that count as MAJOR IMPLEMENTATIONS of that language for this run. Used for every indicator that says 'official', 'first-party', or 'a maintainer of an implementation listed in that language's major_implementations'. Where a language is stewarded by a standards body and separately by the implementation named in frozen_toolchain_recipes, both are official for this benchmark.
official_project_table._major_implementations_rule: 'Major implementation' was previously an undefined, load-bearing phrase in E5, I1, I4, I6, Q6, C5, F5 and the Library Availability index qualification clause (iii). Whether Eclipse counted for Java, Microsoft for C++, or PyPy for Python moved individual metrics by 20 to 80 points and was the scorer's unaided judgement, which this document elsewhere claims to have eliminated. The per-language major_implementations lists below are frozen now, before any language is scored. Selection rule applied identically to all 10: an implementation is listed if it is a separately developed compiler or interpreter for the same language, has a publicly retrievable release within the 24 months before the evidence cutoff, and is acknowledged as an implementation of the language by that language's official documentation or by a recognised standards body for it. The lists may not be expanded, narrowed or reinterpreted at scoring time (global_rules.prohibited_at_scoring_time).

official_docs_root: https://github.com/quidra-lang/quidra (repository documentation, including README, docs/ and any site published from this repository)
major_implementations: quidra-lang/quidra (the reference implementation; the only implementation at the evidence cutoff)

official_project_set: Apple (vendor of the Apple clang toolchain used here)
major_implementations: GCC (the GNU Compiler Collection, GNU Project)

official_project_set: Oracle (publisher of the Java SE Platform and Java Language Specification)
the OpenJS Foundation / Node.js project (the runtime named in the frozen run recipe)
npm, Inc. as operator of the npm registry named by Node.js and TypeScript official documentation
the JVM platform provider for the Kotlin/JVM target used here, namely the OpenJDK project

official_project_table._resolution_procedure_if_a_field_is_wron: If, during evidence collection, a listed root or repository is found not to be the official one for that language at the evidence cutoff, the scorer replaces it with the resource that the language's own official homepage links to as its documentation or source repository, records the substitution and the reason in the evidence record, and applies the same substitution rule to every other language in the same situation. Neither the official_project_set membership nor the major_implementations list may be expanded at scoring time.

evidence_sources._rule: Every indicator names exactly one evidence source id from this table. The same source id means the same kind of evidence for all 10 languages. No language may be scored from a source type that another language was not also examined under.

E1.name: Direct execution on the frozen measurement host
E1.definition: A command executed on the benchmark host (macOS 26.4.1, arm64, Apple M2) using the toolchain version frozen in environment/environment.json and the frozen build/run recipes. Evidence recorded = full command line, exit status, complete stdout and stderr, and the timestamp.

E2.name: Official first-party toolchain and language documentation
E2.definition: Documentation published at a language's official_docs_root as frozen in official_project_table, for the toolchain version under test or the nearest published version, including man pages and built-in --help text shipped by that toolchain. Evidence recorded = exact URL or command, accession timestamp, and a verbatim quoted excerpt supporting the indicator.

E3.name: Official first-party source repository and release history
E3.definition: The repository or repositories listed as official_implementation_repository for the language, including its published releases/tags, its release notes, its governance documents, and its public issue tracker. Evidence recorded = exact URL, accession timestamp, and the specific tag/release/issue identifiers relied on.

E4.name: The language's canonical package index and its self-published package count
E4.definition: The package index selected for that language by the frozen index_selection_rule (see the Library Availability metric). Evidence recorded = index name, index URL, the index's own published total package count (from the index's front page, statistics page, or its documented public API), the exact figure verbatim, and the accession timestamp. If no index satisfies the selection rule for a language, the evidence record states 'no qualifying index at the evidence cutoff' and every E4 indicator for that language is unsatisfied.

E5.name: Official or major-implementation-maintained developer-tool artifact
E5.definition: The published repository, marketplace listing, or official documentation page of a language server (LSP), editor extension, editor grammar, debugger integration, profiler, or debug-adapter integration, where the publisher is a member of that language's official_project_set or is a maintainer of an implementation listed in that language's major_implementations (official_project_table). For the indicators listed in global_rules.tool_admissibility_test.applies_to, the wider three-clause admissibility test governs instead, and the satisfied clause is recorded. Evidence recorded = artifact name, publisher, exact URL, latest release date, accession timestamp, and the verbatim feature statement relied on.

E6.name: Named, citable public production-adoption or population evidence
E6.definition: A publicly retrievable document that names a specific organization, product or population figure: an engineering blog post or documentation page published by the adopting organization itself; an official case-study/user page published by the language's own project; the official documentation or official repository of a shipped product stating its implementation language; or a published, methodologically documented public developer survey or index. Evidence recorded = organization or source name, exact URL, publication date, accession timestamp, and a verbatim quoted excerpt of at most 15 words. Unnamed claims, aggregated impressions, secondhand lists without a primary citation, and undated pages are not admissible.

E7.name: The frozen benchmark source corpus produced by this benchmark run
E7.definition: The Standard-evaluation implementation sources written for this run: all micro-benchmark programs (spec section 12), the SVM implementation (spec section 13), the GMM implementation (spec section 14), and the LightGrad implementation (spec section 15), for that language. Identical workload set for all 10 languages. Evidence recorded = file list with sizes and hashes, plus the computed measurement values.

frozen_probe_sets._rule: These probe sets are frozen here, before any language is scored. Each probe is a small program expressing one language-neutral requirement. The requirement text below is the specification; each language's implementation of it must be the most direct idiomatic expression of that requirement using first-party features only, and must be stored under benchmark/2026-09-17-7677581/standard/rubrics/probes/<probe_id>/<language>.<ext>. A probe that cannot be written for a language using first-party features is recorded as UNSUPPORTED with the reason, and its indicator is unsatisfied. UNSUPPORTED is a real result, never N/A.

probes.requirement: A program that references an identifier that is never declared anywhere.

A program that assigns a value of a textual/string type to a binding declared as an integer type (or the language's nearest equivalent type conflict, if declared types are not available, an operation applying an integer-only operation to a string value).
A program that calls a function declared with two parameters using one argument.
A program with an unbalanced block or grouping delimiter (one opening delimiter without its closing delimiter).
A program that declares a local binding, never reads it, and otherwise compiles and runs correctly.
A program that invokes a member/method name that does not exist on the value's type.
A function declared to return an integer whose return statement returns a textual/string value.
A program that compiles successfully and, at run time, reads element index 10 of a 3-element sequence.

DIAG.capture_rule: Build and run each probe with that language's row in the Diagnostics metric's frozen_diagnostic_configuration (NOT with environment.json's performance recipes), one command per language per that block's one_command_rule. Capture the COMPLETE stderr+stdout. The 'first diagnostic' is the first complete diagnostic message block emitted for the seeded defect. For DIAG-8 the diagnostic is the runtime error/abort message. If a probe produces NO diagnostic at all, every indicator fails for that probe.

probes.requirement: Call the C standard library function cos(double) from the host's system C library and print the result for input 1.0, using only first-party language features and first-party toolchain flags.

Export a function with C calling convention and C-compatible name that takes two 32-bit integers and returns their sum, build it into a linkable artifact, and call it successfully from a C program compiled with clang on this host.

Pass, across the C boundary, (a) a struct containing a 32-bit integer and a double, by value or by pointer with a C-compatible memory layout, and (b) a pointer to a contiguous array of doubles together with its length, and read/modify the array in place without copying it into a language-specific container.

Make the declarations of a supplied C header file usable from the language using a first-party mechanism (direct header import, a first-party binding generator, or an officially published binding tool), without hand-writing the declarations.

Run a fixed CPU-bound workload (sum of sin(i)*sin(i) for i in 0..N, N chosen so the single-worker version takes between 2 and 10 seconds on this host) split across 4 workers using first-party parallelism, and separately with 1 worker. Record wall-clock time for both. Use the median of 5 runs each.
probes.worker_model: A worker may be an OS thread, a process, a lightweight/green thread, or any other parallelism mechanism provided by the language itself or by its first-party standard library, with no third-party package. Shared address space is NOT required. The evidence record must state which mechanism was used for that language. This rule is applied identically to all 10 languages; no language is presumed to pass or to fail it.
probes.identical_across_languages: N, the arithmetic, the number of runs and the 1-vs-4 worker split are identical for all 10 languages. Only the mechanism that supplies the workers differs, and it is recorded.

probes.requirement: A program in which two concurrent workers increment a shared counter without any synchronization, used to check whether the language rejects it at compile time or whether a first-party race detector reports it.

For each of the 24 capabilities enumerated in the Functionality / Expressiveness metric, one minimal program that uses that capability as the capability text describes, compiles (or loads) without error under the frozen recipe, and produces the stated expected output when run. First-party features and first-party standard library only; a capability that requires any package outside the toolchain distribution is UNSUPPORTED for that language.

A program that defines an aggregate type with a named integer field and a named string field, builds a standard-library dynamic array containing 3 such aggregates, calls a function that loops over the array, and prints a checksum. The program must run for at least 2 seconds of CPU time so that a sampling profiler collects samples.
A test suite of exactly 3 tests using the language's first-party test construct or first-party test framework: two that assert a true condition and one that asserts a false condition.
A project of at least two source modules plus one test module, built through the language's first-party build driver from its declarative manifest if one exists.
The complete frozen Standard workload set for that language (E7 corpus), built and run from a clean state on the host, with the package cache emptied before the offline-build check.

A hello-world program built for a non-host target (a target whose OS or CPU architecture differs from macOS/arm64) using only documented first-party target-selection flags, with no additional toolchain installation. Success = a target artifact is produced and the toolchain reports success; execution on the foreign target is not required and is not part of the criterion.

rubric_verification_recipes._rule: FROZEN command lines for rubric verification, one per language per probe family, fixed here before any language is scored. Roughly a third of this document's indicators (V1-V5, DEP-1, FFI-2 to FFI-4, CONC-1, DBG-1 debugger and profiler, PORT-1) cannot be executed from environment.json's frozen_toolchain_recipes, which are single-file build/run invocations. Without this table a literal reading of indicator_model.unverifiable_rule would have recorded every one of those indicators NOT SATISFIED for all 10 languages, silently zeroing Build / Test Integration and capping FFI at what FFI-1 alone can reach; a loose reading would have let each scorer invent commands, so two analysts would compute different numbers. Neither is mechanically reproducible.
rubric_verification_recipes.authority: For the indicators covered here this table supersedes environment.json -> frozen_toolchain_recipes. Everywhere else frozen_toolchain_recipes is unchanged and remains the basis of all performance, size and single-file measurement. No command here may be altered at scoring time (global_rules.prohibited_at_scoring_time).
rubric_verification_recipes.placeholders: Angle-bracketed text (<L>, <TestBundle>, <junit-platform-console-standalone.jar>) marks a value that is read off the probe source or the installed toolchain at run time and recorded verbatim in the evidence record. It is not a licence to change the command. Paths are relative to benchmark/2026-09-17-7677581/standard/rubrics/.

_general_rules.none_entries: A cell reading 'none - ...' records that no admissible command for that task exists for that language at the evidence cutoff, stated NOW rather than discovered at scoring time, with the reason. The named indicator is then unsatisfied by construction. If during evidence collection a documented admissible command IS found, the scorer records the substitution and its evidence under official_project_table._resolution_procedure_if_a_field_is_wrong_or_missing and applies the same correction rule to every other language in the same situation. A 'none' cell is a falsifiable claim, not a verdict.
_general_rules.dep_offline_build: DEP-1's offline build is the same for every language and is therefore not repeated per language: with network access disabled and after the per-language dep_cache_clear command above, build and run EVERY E7 workload for that language using that language's frozen_toolchain_recipes build and run commands. Record every command, exit status and output. Only the cache-clearing command differs per language, because only the cache location differs.
_general_rules.languages_with_no_separate_build_step: For a language whose official toolchain performs NO separate compilation step at all, V1 is satisfied if an admissible driver loads and executes the multi-module project, including its test module, from the project DIRECTORY without naming any source file on the command line. This substitutes 'the project directory' for 'a declarative manifest or project-definition file' only because a language with no build step has nothing to build, and it waives neither conjunct for any language that does compile. It is stated in general terms and is available to any of the 10 languages in that position; it is not an accommodation of a particular language, and a language with a compilation step whose driver simply accepts an entry source file does not qualify.
_general_rules.virtual_machine_targets_and_P3: For a language whose toolchain emits an artifact for a virtual machine or a runtime rather than for an OS/CPU pair, P3 is satisfied only if BOTH: the artifact is produced on this host by the documented command, AND the language's official documentation states that the produced artifact executes on at least one operating-system family or CPU architecture family other than this host's without rebuilding. The documentation sentence is quoted verbatim. Applied identically to Java, Kotlin, TypeScript and to any other of the 10 languages in the same position.
_general_rules.profiler_admissibility: Q4 is governed by its own text: the profiler must be shipped with the toolchain OR named for the language in that language's official documentation (E2). The recipe cells name the profiler that meets that test for each language where one does, and say 'none unless ... cited' where the scorer must supply the naming document. Apple's Instruments/xctrace is named for C++ and Swift because Apple is a member of those two languages' already-frozen official_project_set, not because of anything in this remediation.
_general_rules.identical_probes: The probe SOURCES are the frozen, language-neutral requirements in frozen_probe_sets, identical for all 10 languages. Only the commands that build and run them differ, because only the toolchains differ.

metrics.proxy_statement: THIS IS AN OBJECTIVE PROXY, NOT A HUMAN STUDY. No human subjects were recruited, tested, surveyed or observed for this metric, and no human-comprehension result is claimed, implied or extrapolated anywhere in this benchmark. Per spec section 8 ('Do not fabricate human-study results for metrics such as Readability. If an objective proxy is used, define it explicitly.'), Readability is scored here as a mechanically computable surface-form proxy consisting of two first-party-artifact indicators (existence of a canonical machine-enforced form, and of an official style guide) and four text-geometry measurements taken over the frozen benchmark source corpus (E7). The proxy measures surface regularity and surface complexity of the same algorithms expressed in each language. It does not measure comprehension, learnability, or subjective clarity, and it must never be reported as if it did.
proxy_limitations_to_publish_with_the_sc: The corpus measurements are taken over code authored for this benchmark. They reflect both the language and the authoring of the implementations, even though the same algorithms, inputs and outputs are implemented idiomatically in all 10 languages per spec section 7.
Text geometry is not comprehension. A language may score low on this proxy and still be easy for a human to read, and the reverse.
Thresholds are absolute and were fixed before any measurement; they are not derived from the observed distribution, and no threshold was calibrated against any language's measured value.

R1 AND R3 ARE CORRELATED BY CONSTRUCTION. corpus_definition.preprocessing measures a language that satisfies R1 on canonical-formatter output and a language that does not on hand-written source, and canonical formatters typically enforce a line-length limit, which is what R3 measures. A language with an official formatter therefore gets a second, partly mechanical, chance at R3. This correlation is disclosed rather than removed, because removing R1 from the scored set would delete a real first-party-artifact property that the metric exists to record. It must be published with the score.

The measurement basis differs between languages for the same reason: formatter output for languages satisfying R1, committed sources otherwise. The rule is stated in advance and applied identically, but it is not the same input for every language, and readers should not treat small differences in R3 as pure language properties.

THE TWO BLOCK MODELS ARE NOT ON EXACTLY THE SAME SCALE FOR R4. Under the frozen nesting_depth definition the braces model counts the routine body's own brace pair as depth 1, while the indentation model computes '1 plus the maximum number of indentation steps beyond the routine header', which assigns depth 2 to a routine whose body has a single indentation level and whose braces-model equivalent is depth 1. The indentation model therefore reads approximately one level deeper than the braces model for the same control-flow structure. This affects the two languages whose frozen_lexing_table block_model is 'indentation' - Quidra and Python - and makes R4 marginally HARDER for both of them; it is a measurement artefact, not a language property. It is disclosed rather than corrected, because the correction would raise the measured scores of the language under evaluation and the offset was not among the audit findings; readers must not compare R4 numbers across block models without it. The offset is published with the score.

R5 (sigil density) is MEASURED AND PUBLISHED BUT NO LONGER SCORED. Measuring the definition over ~690 KB of existing C++ (0.188) and over existing Quidra sources (0.171) put both far below the 0.30 threshold, which indicates the indicator is very likely satisfied by all 10 languages and therefore carries no information. It was not re-thresholded, because any tighter threshold could only have been calibrated against values measured from this run's corpora - one of which is Quidra's - which spec 32 forbids. The number is still computed and reported for auditability.

corpus_definition.name: Frozen Readability corpus
corpus_definition.contents: For each language, every Standard-evaluation implementation source file written for this run: all micro benchmarks (spec 12: Fibonacci, factorial, integer arithmetic, floating-point arithmetic, vector inner product, matrix multiplication, sorting, strings, statistics, file I/O, collections), the SVM implementation (spec 13), the GMM implementation (spec 14) and the LightGrad implementation (spec 15).
corpus_definition.identical_across_languages: The workload set is identical for all 10 languages. Build scripts, manifests, generated files, vendored third-party sources and test fixtures are EXCLUDED. Only hand-written implementation sources are included.
corpus_definition.preprocessing: If indicator R1 is satisfied, all four text measurements are taken on the canonical-formatter output. If R1 is not satisfied, they are taken on the committed sources unchanged. This rule is stated in advance and applied identically to all 10 languages.
corpus_definition.if_corpus_incomplete: If a workload could not be implemented in a language, measure over the files that exist and record the missing workloads. If the corpus is empty for a language, R3, R4 and R6 are all unsatisfied and the sigil-density measurement is recorded as 'no corpus'.

measurement_definitions.comment_and_literal_lexing: Taken from the frozen_lexing_table in this metric, which is fixed here before any measurement. It is not read from the evidence record and may not be changed at scoring time. If a table entry is found to contradict a language's official documentation (E2), the scorer applies official_project_table._resolution_procedure_if_a_field_is_wrong_or_missing and records the correction for that language and for every other language in the same situation.
measurement_definitions.code_line: A source line containing at least one non-whitespace character that lies outside a comment.
measurement_definitions.routine: A named callable declaration (function, method, procedure, or equivalent), identified mechanically by that language's routine_header_regex and routine_header_exclusion_regex in frozen_lexing_table, applied to a copy of each line with comments and literals masked out. Anonymous closures are not routines but count toward the nesting depth of the routine that contains them.
measurement_definitions.routine_extent: For a braces block_model: from the routine header line through the line carrying the matching close brace of the block the header opens, inclusive. For an indentation block_model: from the routine header line through the last following line whose indentation exceeds the header's, inclusive.
measurement_definitions.routine_length: The number of code lines within the routine's extent.
measurement_definitions.nesting_depth: For a braces block_model: the maximum number of simultaneously open '{' ... '}' pairs occurring inside the routine's extent, outside comments and literals, with the routine body's own pair counting as depth 1. For an indentation block_model: 1 plus the maximum number of indentation steps by which any code line inside the extent is indented beyond the routine header. This operationalization is frozen here so that no per-language list of 'constructs the official grammar states introduce a nested statement sequence' has to be assembled at scoring time; it is applied identically to all 10 languages.
measurement_definitions.sigil_density: Over all characters of the corpus that are non-whitespace and lie outside comments and outside string/character literals, the fraction that are NOT in the set [A-Za-z0-9_]. Measured and reported; not scored (see proxy_limitations).
measurement_definitions.percentile: p95 is the nearest-rank 95th percentile: sort the values ascending and take the value at 1-based index ceil(0.95 * n). Median is the 50th percentile computed as the mean of the two central values when n is even. Both are computed over ALL routines of that language's corpus, pooled across files.
measurement_definitions.reference_implementation: A single measurement script implementing these definitions is stored at benchmark/2026-09-17-7677581/scripts/readability_proxy.py and is run unchanged for all 10 languages; its output is the evidence. The script takes its per-language lexing table from this document's frozen_lexing_table rather than from a table of its own, so the two cannot diverge. It exists as of this remediation - it did not when the document was first frozen, which left R3, R4 and R6 mechanically undetermined. Invocation: `python3 scripts/readability_proxy.py --rubrics methodology/05_standard_rubrics.json --language <name> --corpus <dir>`, repeated per language with the same flags and the same script.
measurement_definitions.reference_implementation_integrity_rule: Before any language is measured the scorer recomputes the SHA-256 of readability_proxy.py and compares it with the value above. A mismatch stops scoring; the script may not be edited during scoring. If a defect is found in it, the defect and the fix are recorded in methodology/CORRECTIONS.md, the new hash replaces the value above, and EVERY language is re-measured with the corrected script.

indicators.text: A canonical automatic code formatter for the language is published by a member of the language's official_project_set, and running it over the frozen corpus succeeds and is idempotent (a second run produces byte-identical output).
A member of the language's official_project_set publishes a written style and/or naming-convention guide as a documentation artifact (not merely a formatter).
Over the frozen corpus: median code-line length <= 80 characters AND 95th-percentile code-line length <= 120 characters.
Over the frozen corpus: median per-routine maximum nesting depth <= 4 AND 95th-percentile per-routine maximum nesting depth <= 5.

Over the frozen corpus: sigil density <= 0.30. MEASURED AND PUBLISHED BUT NOT SCORED - this indicator does not contribute to the level (see proxy_limitations and the remediation_changelog entry for finding 7).
Over the frozen corpus: median routine length <= 30 code lines AND 95th-percentile routine length <= 60 code lines.

metrics.scoring_procedure: Count the satisfied indicators among the FIVE SCORED indicators R1, R2, R3, R4 and R6, and award the matching level. R5 is measured and reported but contributes nothing to the count. No other input may affect the score.

levels.name: Canonical and low-surface-complexity
levels.criteria: All 5 scored indicators satisfied: canonical official formatter (idempotent on the corpus), official style guide, and the three corpus measurements within their frozen thresholds.

levels.name: Strong
levels.criteria: Exactly 4 of the 5 scored indicators satisfied.

levels.name: Adequate
levels.criteria: Exactly 3 of the 5 scored indicators satisfied.

levels.name: Mixed
levels.criteria: Exactly 2 of the 5 scored indicators satisfied.

levels.name: Weak
levels.criteria: Exactly 1 of the 5 scored indicators satisfied.

metrics.top_level_evidence_required: To award 100 the evidence record must contain: (a) the exact formatter command executed on the host, its exit status, and the diff proving byte-identical output on a second run; (b) the URL and a verbatim excerpt of the official style guide; (c) the readability_proxy.py output showing median and p95 line length, median and p95 nesting depth, median and p95 routine length, and the measured sigil density (reported, not scored), each compared against its frozen threshold; and (d) the recomputed SHA-256 of readability_proxy.py matching measurement_definitions.reference_implementation_sha256. Any missing item forbids 100.
metrics.na_policy: Never N/A. A language with no formatter, no style guide, and corpus measurements outside all thresholds scores 0.

frozen_lexing_table._rule: Frozen before measurement. Regular expressions are Python 're' syntax and are applied to a copy of each line in which comments, string literals and character literals have already been masked out. block_model selects which nesting_depth and routine_extent rule applies. The table is data for readability_proxy.py; the script contains no per-language logic of its own.

metrics.indicator_change_note: R4 and R6 were changed from 'no routine exceeds N' to a 95th-percentile statistic because a single outlier routine in benchmark-authored code flipped the whole indicator, and the outlier is a property of the authoring rather than of the language. R5 was retired from scoring, and the id was deliberately NOT reused or renumbered, so that downstream references to R1-R6 still resolve. Retiring R5 is score-neutral if, as the pre-freeze measurement suggests, every language satisfies it: the old bands over 6 indicators with R5 always satisfied and the new bands over the 5 scored indicators map every language to the same level.

metrics.definition: The number of capabilities from a fixed, language-neutral, 24-item general-purpose-programming capability checklist that the language supports using first-party features and its first-party standard library only.
metrics.neutrality_note: The 24 capabilities were selected to span the mainstream language families represented in the fixed comparison set (dynamic scripting, systems, managed/VM, functional-influenced, and ahead-of-time compiled). No item was added because Quidra has it, and no item was removed because Quidra lacks it. Items that Quidra may fail remain in the list.
metrics.overlap_declaration: X19 (a standard-library concurrency primitive) is also an input to the Concurrency metric. Functionality / Expressiveness and Concurrency are BOTH members of the Language / Development category, so this is a double count WITHIN a single category, not across two: concurrency capability contributes to 2 of that category's 8 equally weighted metrics (Code Efficiency / Conciseness, Readability, Functionality / Expressiveness, Diagnostics, Dependency Simplicity, Portability, FFI / Interoperability, Concurrency), i.e. to 25% of the category rather than 12.5%. X22 (a unit-test construct shipped with the toolchain distribution) is a narrower test than Build / Test Integration's V2, which after the widening in global_rules.tool_admissibility_test counts any admissible test framework rather than only a toolchain-shipped one; the two overlap partly, and a language whose only admissible test framework is third-party can satisfy V2 while failing X22. Both overlaps are declared in advance and are NOT adjusted for, because spec 8.1 fixes equal within-category weights and forbids post-hoc metric-membership changes. They must be restated wherever the Language / Development category score is published.

capability_checklist.capability: User-defined product type with named fields (struct, record, class, or equivalent), constructible and field-accessible.

User-defined sum type / tagged union with case analysis that the toolchain checks for exhaustiveness, or, if exhaustiveness is not checked, a first-party tagged-union type with a documented discriminant.
Parametric polymorphism: a type or routine parameterized over a type parameter, instantiable at two different argument types.
Interface / protocol / trait-style abstraction with dynamic dispatch through a value whose concrete type is chosen at run time.
First-class functions and closures that capture a variable from the enclosing scope.
Pattern matching or destructuring binding that decomposes an aggregate into its components in a single binding form.
A user-definable iterator/generator/sequence abstraction consumable by the language's own loop or iteration construct.

A first-class error-signalling and handling construct with propagation across call frames (exceptions, or result/error values with a propagation operator or documented propagation idiom in the standard library).
A deterministic resource-cleanup construct that runs cleanup on scope exit including on the error path (destructors/RAII, defer, try-with-resources, context manager, or equivalent).
Operator overloading or user-defined behaviour for at least one built-in operator on a user-defined type.
Compile-time or load-time constant evaluation of a non-trivial expression, documented as guaranteed by the language (a constant expression evaluated before run time).
First-party metaprogramming: macros, compile-time code generation, or runtime reflection over program structure.
Modules or namespaces with explicit import and at least two visibility levels (public and non-public).
Standard library provides all three of: growable array/list, hash map/dictionary, and set.

Standard library provides Unicode-aware string handling: documented Unicode text representation and at least one Unicode-aware operation (case mapping, normalization, or codepoint/grapheme iteration).
Constraints or bounds on type parameters (trait bounds, where-clauses, interface constraints, type classes, or equivalent) enforced by the toolchain.
IEEE-754 double-precision floating point with a standard-library math set of at least sqrt, exp, log and the trigonometric functions.
Standard library file I/O and filesystem operations: read a file, write a file, and query path existence.
Standard library concurrency primitive of any kind (thread, task, coroutine, process, or async runtime).
First-party standard-library serialization to and from a structured textual data format (JSON or an equivalent documented structured format).
First-party standard-library regular expressions with match and capture-group extraction.
First-party unit-test construct or test framework shipped with the toolchain distribution.
A non-copying view/slice over a contiguous sequence, where mutating through the view is observable in the original storage.
Arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic in the standard library, OR documented fixed-width integer semantics together with a standard-library checked or wrapping arithmetic API.

metrics.verification_rule: A capability is supported only if its EXPR probe for that language compiles/loads without error under the frozen recipe and produces the expected output when run on the host (E1), AND the feature used is documented in that language's official documentation (E2). A capability that requires any package outside the toolchain distribution is NOT supported. Record the probe path, the command, the output, and the documentation URL for each supported capability, and the reason for each unsupported one.
metrics.scoring_procedure: Let S = number of supported capabilities out of 24. Award the level whose band contains S.

levels.name: Comprehensive
levels.criteria: S >= 22 of 24 capabilities supported with first-party features only.

metrics.top_level_evidence_required: To award 100 the evidence record must list at least 22 capability ids, each with: the probe source path, the exact build/run command, the captured successful output, and the official documentation URL with a verbatim excerpt naming the feature. Capabilities claimed from documentation alone, without an executed probe, do not count.
metrics.na_policy: Never N/A. Unsupported capabilities are counted as unsupported and lower the score.

metrics.definition: The information content and machine-consumability of the diagnostics that the language's frozen toolchain emits for a fixed set of 8 seeded single-defect programs.
metrics.aggregation_rule: Each of D1-D5 is evaluated per probe and is SATISFIED for the language only if it holds for at least 6 of the 8 DIAG probes. D6 is a single toolchain-level check. Probes that emit no diagnostic at all count as failing every per-probe indicator.

indicators.text: The first diagnostic states the source file, the line number, and the column (or character offset) of the defect. A NUMERIC column or character offset must be printed; a caret or source-excerpt indication alone satisfies D2 but does not satisfy D1.
The first diagnostic reproduces the offending source line or a source excerpt/caret indication pointing at the defect.
The first diagnostic carries a stable machine-readable diagnostic identifier (an error/warning code or named rule) that is documented in the official documentation.
The first diagnostic names the specific program entities involved: the offending identifier by name, and/or both conflicting types spelled out, rather than only a generic category.
The first diagnostic includes at least one actionable help/note/suggestion/fix line that states what to do, distinct from restating the error.

The toolchain emits its diagnostics in a structured machine-readable format (JSON, SARIF, or equivalent) via a flag or mode documented in the official documentation; verified by executing it on DIAG-2 and parsing the output successfully.

metrics.scoring_procedure: Count the satisfied indicators among D1-D6 and award the matching level.

levels.name: Minimal or absent
levels.criteria: 0 or 1 of D1-D6 satisfied, which includes any language whose toolchain emits no diagnostic for 3 or more of the 8 probes.

metrics.top_level_evidence_required: To award 100 the evidence record must contain the complete captured diagnostic text for all 8 probes, a per-probe yes/no table for D1-D5 showing at least 6 of 8 for each, the documentation URL for the diagnostic-code scheme (D3), and the structured-output command plus the successfully parsed machine-readable diagnostic (D6).
metrics.na_policy: Never N/A. A toolchain that reports defects without location, entity names or suggestions receives the low level.

frozen_diagnostic_configuration._rule: The exact toolchain configuration used for the 8 DIAG probes, frozen here before any language is scored. It applies to the DIAG probe set ONLY; every other measurement uses the frozen recipes unchanged.
frozen_diagnostic_configuration.why: The frozen build recipes carry no warning configuration at all (clang++ -std=c++20 -O2 with no -Wall, tsc with no --strict, javac with no -Xlint), and no indicator 'explicitly requires' a warning flag. DIAG-5 (an unused local that otherwise compiles) would therefore have produced no diagnostic at all for several languages, failing D1-D5 for that probe on a FLAG CHOICE rather than on diagnostic quality, while a language that makes the same defect an error by default passed. That is a measurement of this document's own configuration, not of the toolchain. It is also the specific asymmetry spec section 7 warns about: comparing one language's always-on checking against another language's checks-disabled release configuration.
frozen_diagnostic_configuration.principle: ONE principle, applied to all 10: use the configuration that the language's OWN official documentation presents as the normal development configuration, for BOTH the warning configuration and the optimization/build mode. Where the official documentation presents the default as the normal development configuration, the default is used and no flag is added. The chosen configuration and the documentation sentence that justifies it are recorded per language with URL and verbatim excerpt.
frozen_diagnostic_configuration.optimization_mode_rule: The performance-oriented optimization flags carried by environment.json -> frozen_toolchain_recipes (-O2, -O, -OReleaseFast) are NOT used for the DIAG probe set, for any language. Those flags exist to measure speed, and DIAG measures diagnostics. Carrying them here would have compared one language's always-on checking against another language's checks-disabled release build: DIAG-8 (reading index 10 of a 3-element sequence) produces a trapping, located runtime diagnostic in a toolchain's default development mode and no diagnostic at all in a release mode that elides bounds checking. Each language therefore uses its own documented default or documented development build mode, which is the same principle already applied to the warning configuration and is applied identically to all 10.
frozen_diagnostic_configuration.one_command_rule: EXACTLY ONE compile-or-check command per language supplies the diagnostic text scored for D1-D5. No language may have two commands tried and the better output taken. D6's structured machine-readable output may be produced by a different documented flag or mode, is executed separately, and counts for D6 only; it may not supply text for D1-D5 for any language.

configurations.Quidra: quidra build FILE.qui -o BIN   (documented default build mode; no warning-configuration flag is documented). `quidra check --json` is a separate documented mode executed for D6 only and supplies no D1-D5 text, per one_command_rule.
configurations.Python: python3 -X dev FILE.py   (Python Development Mode, documented as the development configuration)
configurations.C++: clang++ -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra FILE.cpp -o BIN   (default optimization mode per optimization_mode_rule)
configurations.Rust: rustc FILE.rs -o BIN   (documented default build mode and default lint set)
configurations.Swift: swiftc FILE.swift -o BIN   (documented default build mode, -Onone)
configurations.Zig: zig build-exe FILE.zig -femit-bin=BIN   (documented default build mode, Debug)

frozen_diagnostic_configuration.runtime_probe: DIAG-8 is a runtime probe. It is BUILT with that language's row above and RUN with that language's frozen run recipe; the built artifact is the one the row produces, not a release-mode artifact. For a language with no separate build step the row above is itself the run command.
frozen_diagnostic_configuration.recording: Every DIAG command is recorded verbatim with exit status, complete stdout and stderr. A language whose recorded command differs from its row here invalidates that language's Diagnostics score.
frozen_diagnostic_configuration.symmetry: Four of the ten rows add a warning flag and six use the documented default, decided by each language's own documentation rather than by which languages benefit. Any of the 10 could have landed in either group. Every row uses that language's own documented default build mode, so no language is measured in a checks-disabled configuration while another is measured with its checking on.

metrics.definition: How little external dependency machinery is required to build and run the complete frozen Standard workload set in the language, measured as the number of distinct non-toolchain packages required plus the reproducibility properties of obtaining them.

measured_quantities.D_total: The number of DISTINCT packages, direct plus transitive, that are required to build and run the complete frozen Standard workload corpus (E7) for that language and that are NOT installed by the toolchain distribution present on this host. Determined by resolving the workload's declared dependencies with the language's own package mechanism and counting distinct package identities (name, ignoring version). Publisher identity is irrelevant: a package published by the language's own project still counts if it is not part of the installed toolchain distribution. Standard-library modules that ship with the toolchain count as 0.
measured_quantities.offline_build: Whether the complete workload set builds successfully with the package cache emptied and with network access disabled (or, equivalently, with the toolchain's documented offline flag). Verified on the host.
measured_quantities.pinning: Whether the language's own package mechanism can pin exact resolved versions of all transitive dependencies for reproducible rebuild (lockfile, vendoring, or documented exact-pin manifest), per official documentation.
measured_quantities.install_units: The number of separately installable components that had to be present on this host to compile AND run the workload set. COUNTING RULE: a single downloadable distribution that provides both compilation and execution of the corpus counts as 1; a language whose compiler requires a separately downloaded runtime or SDK to execute the corpus counts as 2. The count is frozen per language in install_units_table below.

install_units_table._rule: Frozen before scoring, applying the counting rule above to environment/environment.json -> toolchains and the frozen recipes. Freezing it removes the only live variable this metric had, which would otherwise have been decided at scoring time for exactly the ambiguous cases that determine the result.

_notes.Quidra: the quidra binary compiles and runs the corpus.
_notes.Python: the CPython distribution runs the corpus; there is no separate build component.
_notes.C++: the Apple clang toolchain (Xcode Command Line Tools) provides the compiler and the C++ runtime.
_notes.Rust: the rustc distribution provides compilation and the produced binaries are self-contained.
_notes.Go: the Go distribution provides compilation and the produced binaries are self-contained.
_notes.Java: the JDK provides both javac and java.
_notes.TypeScript: tsc compiles and node executes; two separately downloaded distributions.
_notes.Kotlin: kotlinc compiles and a separately downloaded JRE/JDK executes.
_notes.Swift: the Swift toolchain provides swiftc and the Swift runtime.
_notes.Zig: the Zig distribution provides compilation and the produced binaries are self-contained.

install_units_table._correction_rule: If evidence collection shows a count here is wrong under the counting rule, the scorer records the correction and its evidence under official_project_table._resolution_procedure_if_a_field_is_wrong_or_missing and re-checks every other language against the same rule.

metrics.expected_discrimination_note: Spec section 7 bars outsourcing the core computation to external libraries, so the E7 corpus is standard-library-only for every language. D_total is therefore EXPECTED to be 0 for all 10, and this metric is expected to collapse onto install_units and offline_build. The resulting near-uniform scores must be published with this sentence: 'Dependency Simplicity is near-uniform by construction under a standard-library-only corpus; the remaining differences reflect how each vendor packages its downloads, not a measured difference in dependency complexity.' Readers must not read the spread as an ecosystem measurement. Note also that this is the one Language / Development metric on which a rich library ecosystem can only be a liability, which structurally favours a language that has none; that is a property of the metric as specified in spec section 8 and is disclosed rather than corrected here.
metrics.scoring_procedure: Compute D_total, offline_build, pinning and install_units. FIRST apply the override in level 0: if the workload set cannot be built at all on this host and the language provides no documented way to pin or reproduce the dependency resolution it requires, the score is 0 regardless of every other criterion. Otherwise award the highest level whose criteria are fully met, testing levels from 100 downward.

levels.name: Self-contained single unit
levels.criteria: D_total = 0 AND offline_build succeeds AND install_units = 1 (one official distribution provides both compilation and execution of the workload set).

levels.name: Self-contained, multiple install units
levels.criteria: D_total = 0 AND offline_build succeeds AND install_units >= 2.

levels.name: Few pinned dependencies
levels.criteria: 1 <= D_total <= 3 AND pinning is available AND offline_build succeeds after a single initial fetch.

levels.name: Moderate pinned dependency graph
levels.criteria: 4 <= D_total <= 10 AND pinning is available AND offline_build succeeds after a single initial fetch.

levels.name: Large or unpinned dependency graph
levels.criteria: 11 <= D_total <= 50, OR (1 <= D_total <= 50 AND pinning is not available), OR (1 <= D_total <= 50 AND offline_build fails), OR (D_total = 0 AND offline_build fails).

levels.name: Unbounded or unresolvable
levels.criteria: D_total > 50, OR the workload set cannot be built at all on this host without dependency resolution that the language provides no documented way to pin or reproduce (this second clause is an override applied before the downward level test, per scoring_procedure).

exhaustiveness_verification.defect_corrected: The level set was NOT exhaustive, contradicting global_rules.application_order.5 ('Levels are mutually exclusive and exhaustive by construction'). The case D_total = 0 AND offline_build FAILS matched no level: 100 and 80 both require offline_build to succeed, 60/40/20 all required D_total >= 1, and 0 required D_total > 50 or an unpinnable-dependency build failure, which cannot arise at D_total = 0. A language whose standard-library-only corpus builds online but fails the cache-emptied offline check - a realistic outcome for any toolchain that touches the network on a first build - left the scorer with no defined score and therefore a free judgement call, which spec 25.4 prohibits.
exhaustiveness_verification.method: Every combination of (D_total band) x (pinning) x (offline_build) x (install_units) was enumerated against the amended criteria and checked for exactly one match.
cases: D_total = 0, offline fails, any pinning, any install_units -> 20 (unique, via the clause added by this remediation)
1 <= D_total <= 3, pinning available, offline succeeds after one fetch -> 60 (unique)
4 <= D_total <= 10, pinning available, offline succeeds after one fetch -> 40 (unique)
4 <= D_total <= 10, pinning unavailable OR offline fails -> 20 (unique)
11 <= D_total <= 50, any pinning, any offline outcome -> 20 (unique; the first clause of level 20 matches and no higher level's D_total band does)
workload set unbuildable with unpinnable/unreproducible resolution, any D_total -> 0 by the level-0 override, applied first
exhaustiveness_verification.result: Every case matches exactly one level. pinning and install_units are irrelevant at D_total = 0 except for the 100-vs-80 step, and install_units is irrelevant at D_total >= 1; both facts are intended and are stated here so no scorer supplies a rule of their own.

metrics.top_level_evidence_required: To award 100 the evidence record must contain: the full dependency-resolution output or an explicit statement plus command proving zero non-toolchain packages; the exact offline build command, the cache-clearing command preceding it, and its successful exit status; and the list of installed components from environment/environment.json showing a single official distribution covering both build and run.
metrics.na_policy: Never N/A. A language whose workloads require a large unpinnable dependency graph receives the low level; a language that needs none receives the high level.

metrics.definition: The breadth of officially supported platforms for the toolchain, the presence of documented cross-target support, the platform independence of the first-party standard library, and implementation independence of the language definition.

indicators.text: A member of the language's official_project_set publishes ready-to-install toolchain builds (installers, archives or release assets) for at least 3 distinct operating-system families.
Those official builds cover at least 2 distinct CPU architecture families (for example x86-64 and AArch64).

The installed toolchain can produce an artifact for a target whose OS or CPU architecture differs from the host, using only documented first-party target-selection flags and no additional toolchain installation; verified by building probe PORT-1 on the host.
Official documentation publishes an explicit platform-support list that names supported platforms and their support status (for example a tiered support table or a supported-platforms page).
The first-party standard library documents platform-independent APIs for ALL FOUR of: file input/output, filesystem path manipulation, clock/time, and environment-variable or process access.

A normative language specification exists that EITHER the implementation's own documentation designates as normative and that contains a conformance statement, OR is published by a standards body independent of the implementation.
At least two independently developed implementations of the language exist and are acknowledged by official documentation.

metrics.indicator_change_note: The former single indicator P6 accepted 'a published language specification/reference standard that an independent implementation could be written against' with no normativity, conformance or independence test. Markdown about a language, self-published in that language's own implementation repository and reviewed by nobody outside it, satisfied it on its face and scored identically to ISO/IEC 14882 or the Java Language Specification. P6 is therefore split into P6a (normativity or independent publication) and P6b (implementation independence in fact), each carrying the same weight as every other Portability indicator, and the level bands are recomputed over 7 indicators. The scorer records which of the two each language satisfies. Any of the 10 languages can satisfy either, both or neither.
metrics.scoring_procedure: Count the satisfied indicators among P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6a and P6b (7 indicators) and award the matching level.

levels.name: Multi-OS, multi-architecture, cross-targeting, normatively specified and independently implemented

metrics.top_level_evidence_required: To award 100 the evidence record must contain: the official download/release URLs enumerating OS families and architectures (P1, P2); the exact cross-target build command from rubric_verification_recipes executed on the host with its successful exit status, the produced artifact path and a file-type identification of that artifact showing the foreign target, or, for a virtual-machine artifact, the documentation sentence required by rubric_verification_recipes._general_rules.virtual_machine_targets_and_P3 (P3); the platform-support page URL with a verbatim excerpt (P4); four standard-library documentation URLs, one per required API area (P5); the specification URL together with the designation-as-normative statement and the conformance statement, or the independent standards body's publication (P6a); and the official acknowledgement of at least two independently developed implementations (P6b).
metrics.na_policy: Never N/A. A language available only for the host platform receives the low level. A language with only one implementation and only a self-published, non-normative description of itself fails P6a and P6b and loses those two indicators; no allowance is made for the language's age.

metrics.definition: The ability, using first-party features only, to call into and be called from the platform C ABI, to exchange aggregate and array data across that boundary without copying, to consume existing C declarations mechanically, and to interoperate with at least one further non-C ecosystem.

indicators.text: Probe FFI-1 builds and runs successfully on the host using only first-party features and documented first-party flags, printing the correct value of cos(1.0) to at least 6 significant digits.
Probe FFI-2 builds successfully and the resulting symbol is callable from a C program compiled with clang on this host, returning the correct sum.
The FFI mechanism used by F1 and F2 is documented in the language's official documentation, including how foreign types map to language types.

Probe FFI-3 builds and runs successfully: a mixed-field struct crosses the C boundary with a C-compatible layout, and a pointer+length array of doubles is modified in place across the boundary with the modification observable on the other side, without copying into a language-specific container.

Probe FFI-4 succeeds: C declarations from a supplied header become usable through a first-party mechanism (direct header import, a binding generator shipped with the toolchain, or a binding generator published by a member of the official_project_set), without hand-writing the declarations.

Official documentation describes first-party interoperation with at least one additional non-C ecosystem or ABI (for example the JVM, .NET, Objective-C/Swift runtime, JavaScript/WASM, or Python's C-API), AND the corresponding target, flag or feature is present in the installed toolchain on this host.

metrics.scoring_procedure: Count the satisfied indicators among F1-F6 and award the matching level.

levels.name: Closed
levels.criteria: 0 or 1 of F1-F6 satisfied, which includes any language that cannot call a C library function with first-party features.

metrics.top_level_evidence_required: To award 100 the evidence record must contain, for each of FFI-1 through FFI-4: the probe source path, the exact build and run commands, the exit statuses and the captured correct output; plus the official FFI documentation URL with a verbatim excerpt of the type-mapping rules (F3); plus, for F6, the documentation URL for the additional ecosystem and the host command output proving the target/flag exists in the installed toolchain.
metrics.na_policy: Never N/A. A language with no first-party foreign-function capability receives 0 rather than N/A, because this metric intentionally tests that capability.

metrics.definition: First-party support for parallel execution, synchronization, message passing, asynchronous concurrency, data-race detection or prevention, and structured task parallelism.

indicators.text: Probe CONC-1 demonstrates real parallel speedup with first-party features only: median wall-clock time of the 4-worker version <= median wall-clock time of the 1-worker version divided by 1.5, on this 8-logical-CPU host, with both versions producing the same numeric result. The worker mechanism is any admitted by CONC-1.worker_model and is recorded.
